**No. dp is not iteratively converged on any of the grids, so I can't give a trustworthy mesh-independent value or uncertainty.**

**Why "SIMPLE solution converged" doesn't help here:** every run stopped because the residual tolerances in `fvSolution` were met (p 1e-2, U/k/ε 1e-3). Those tolerances are loose, and stopping on them doesn't mean dp had stopped changing. The `multiFieldValue.dat` histories show dp still drifting slowly up and down when each run ended:

| Grid | Iterations | dp in the last ~10% (the averaging window) | What it's doing at the end |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12k | 279 | about −5.45 to −5.66 | turning back after a swing between −5.0 and −5.66 |
| 28k | 440 | about −4.58 to −5.10 | stalling after a rise from −6.08 to −4.58 |
| 62k | 811 | about −4.50 to −5.45 | rising steadily, about 0.02 per iteration |
| 139k | 1419 | about −2.97 to −4.06 | falling steadily, about 0.01 per iteration |

On the finest grid, dp swings between about −2.6 and −4.1 within the last ~300 iterations. That's an iterative error of roughly ±0.7 m²/s², about 20–40% of dp. The 139k log also shows repeated "bounding epsilon" and pressure residuals stuck at about 5e-3, so it is stalled, not settling.

**Effect on the grid study:** the window-mean dp values, finest to coarsest, come out at roughly −3.5, −5.0, −4.7 and −5.6. These are approximate; I read them off the tails of the data rather than computing them exactly. The sequence isn't monotonic, and the differences between grids (about 1–1.5) are the same size as the drift within each run. So the differences are mostly iterative noise caught at different points in each swing, not discretisation error. Richardson extrapolation or a GCI on these numbers would be meaningless. A "last 10% mean" is also unreliable when the window covers only part of a slow swing.

**To fix this:**
1. Rerun each level with much tighter residual targets (e.g. p 1e-5, others 1e-6), or turn off `residualControl` and run until dp is flat.
2. If the 139k case still won't settle, look at what's driving the swing: the bounding of ε, the relaxation factors, or a physically unsteady recirculation zone that may need a transient (pimpleFoam) approach.
3. Average dp over several full swings, or better, require dp to be steady to well below the expected difference between grids.
4. Only then do the Richardson extrapolation / GCI across the four grids.

FINAL: converged=no; value=none; uncertainty=none
